L13·N4208unmasked layer
This neuron has an almost entirely negative, near-flat response; its highest values come at the `<|begin_of_text|>` token and the ordinary words immediately following it at the very start of a document, while mid-document tokens (e.g. inside long legal/press-release sentences) push it to its most negative — i.e. it is a document-start/position detector rather than a semantic one.

L16·N8169unmasked layer
Fires on the leading digit-chunk of a multi-token numeral — e.g. the "3" in "3.4.1", "10" in "10.21%", "200" in "2001", "130" in "1300 South" (also the space/paren just before such a number) — i.e. a numeric token that is immediately continued by more digits; it is strongly *suppressed* when the token in that same pre-number slot is a word/letter string (" Windows 3.4", " CC3000", "The Family of 4").

L22·N8481unmasked layer
This neuron is only weakly selective: it peaks on ordinary mid-sentence continuation tokens (function/filler words like "that", "an", "rest", "choose", or a sub-word/name piece such as "l" in "Athlone", "Brigade") where the next content is fresh/unpredictable, and is strongly *suppressed* at formulaic/repetition points — an acronym about to be expanded ("stands for", "AHAM -"), a repeated question ending in "?", or duplicated boilerplate ("contact us for quote").
